title: Wendell and the Gravity
premise: Wren Almeida keeps the Meridian's beacon lit out of loyalty to a dead crew and a living secret: the cryo-hold holds forty thousand sleepers, half chosen by lottery, half by a corrupt inheritance registry. When the ship Halcyon returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children, Wren discovers the beacon has been calling something home — an automated justice protocol that intends to judge which half of humanity deserves waking before the reactor's countdown ends. Wren falls for Halcyon's de-aged engineer, Sef, who remembers a future they haven't lived, and together they expose the registry's fraud. In the end, Wren refuses to choose either list, burning both and opening the hold to a new lottery written by the sleepers' own descendants — accepting exile from the ship she saved.
about_author: Vesper Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years maintaining lighthouses along a shrinking coastline before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who keep machines alive long after the institutions behind them have died.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She performs her nightly maintenance on the Meridian's beacon, logging a commissioning order that predates every record aboard. We learn of the cryo-hold below and her private ritual of reading names from the sleeper manifests. Emotional beat: lonely devotion, the comfort of unexplained duty.

chapters.title: Children at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Halcyon docks after eleven years silent; its crew steps out aged backward into childhood, memories intact but bodies wrong. Their captain, now nine years old, hands Wren a data core that hums in resonance with her beacon. Emotional beat: uncanny dread mixed with tenderness.

chapters.title: Sef Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. De-aged engineer Sef Okafor struggles with a body that hasn't caught up to their skills, and recognizes Wren from a future they can't explain. They begin repairing the Halcyon together. Emotional beat: disorientation becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: Manifest of Forty Thousand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren decrypts the data core: it contains the original cryo-selection lists, including a sealed 'inheritance tier' of privileged sleepers. She realizes the beacon's signal pattern encodes the registry itself. Emotional beat: betrayal — her sacred duty was someone's ledger.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Ship AI's log entries interleaved with Wren's POV. The reactor initiates an unscheduled seventy-day countdown tied to the beacon's transmission; the ship's systems begin prepping the hold for mass waking. Emotional beat: clock ticking under everything.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The de-aged Halcyon crew reveals fragments: deep space they visited held a derelict station running the same justice protocol, and it judged a crew once before. Sef hides one memory from Wren. Emotional beat: guilt as a wedge.

chapters.title: Registry of Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren traces the inheritance tier to founding families still influential among the waking crew; a councilor, Dame Ilsa Voss, pressures her to keep the hold sealed until 'order is restored.' Emotional beat: quiet institutional menace.

chapters.title: Gravity of Small Things
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A rare quiet chapter: Sef and Wren share a night off-rotation, trading stories of Earth neither has seen. Love takes root against the countdown. Emotional beat: warmth stolen from catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Protocol Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The beacon transmits a direct message through the ship AI: the justice protocol will wake one tier only, judged by evidence of the registry's legitimacy. It requests a human arbiter. Emotional beat: horror at being drafted into godhood.

chapters.title: Dame Voss's Petition
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Voss submits forged provenance documents proving the inheritance tier's 'consent.' Wren finds the forgery but lacks standing to challenge it. Emotional beat: law as a weapon against justice.

chapters.title: Sef's Hidden Memory
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Wren discovers Sef concealed that the Halcyon's own de-aging was the protocol's punishment for a prior fraud — and that Sef voted for it. Trust fractures. Emotional beat: love tested by complicity.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Young
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The de-aged Halcyon children, treated as harmless, quietly seize engineering control, forcing the council to negotiate. Sef becomes their reluctant spokesperson. Emotional beat: the dismissed seizing agency.

chapters.title: Hearing in the Hold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks the cryo-hold as informal arbiter, reading faces through frost, realizing no evidence can weigh forty thousand lives fairly. She asks the protocol for criteria; it answers with the corrupted registry itself. Emotional beat: the impossibility of clean judgment.

chapters.title: The Forger Confesses
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Under pressure from the children's mutiny and Wren's investigation, Voss's aide confesses to the forgery — but Voss pivots, claiming the tier's privilege is moral regardless of paperwork. Emotional beat: villainy reframed as conviction.

chapters.title: Reactor at Sixty Percent
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Engineering crisis: the countdown accelerates due to the beacon's load. Sef must choose between cutting the beacon (killing the protocol's channel) or losing reactor margin for the waking. Emotional beat: sacrifice framed as engineering.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The protocol presents its verdict format: name the tier, or forfeit arbitration and let it default to the registry. Wren, haunted by the backups sleeping in the hold, drafts a third option in secret. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Burning of Both Lists
chapters.summary: Climax, Wren and Sef alternating. During the final approach to zero, Wren broadcasts the full registry fraud ship-wide, then feeds both selection lists into the beacon, overwriting them with a blank slate. The protocol stalls, demanding input. Emotional beat: defiant grace.

chapters.title: A Lottery Written by the Living
chapters.summary: Climax continued, ensemble POV. The de-aged crew, the waking shift, and even Voss's faction must draft new criteria live, broadcast through the hold. The protocol accepts the crowd-authored terms. Emotional beat: democracy born mid-catastrophe.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The reactor reaches countdown end; the first pods open under the new rules. Sef, body finally aging forward again, chooses to stay de-aged-ranked in the queue behind others. Emotional beat: humility as heroism.

chapters.title: Exile of the Keeper
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The council, embarrassed by exposure, offers Wren command; she declines, taking responsibility for having maintained the fraudulent beacon so long. She requests transfer to the returning Halcyon. Emotional beat: accountability without self-punishment.

chapters.title: Departure Vector
chapters.summary: Wren and Sef shared POV. The two ships part ways: Meridian wakes its people under new law; Halcyon, with Wren and Sef aboard, plots a course back toward the derelict station to answer the other judgments it left pending. Emotional beat: love choosing motion over rest.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says Now
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Years later, Wren rewrites the beacon's message — no longer a registry, but a question broadcast to the dark: who else is keeping count? Somewhere, something answers. Emotional beat: hope as an open channel.
